title: SIMBAD: Spatio-Temporal Traffic Forecasting Robust to Aperiodicity
topic: Data-centric AI->Data-centric AI methods and tools
claim: Periodic patterns break down for irregular events, and baseline error grows as aperiodicity increases while ours stays robust.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, line plot then two scatter plots
description: Three side-by-side plots in blue and orange. Panel (a) is a line chart of traffic flow over 24 hours for two sensors on two dates. Sensor 123 follows the same pattern on both days. Sensor 137 matches the earlier day (blue) but drops sharply on the later day (orange), so connected nodes show diverging periodic patterns. Panel (b) is a dense blue scatter of the L1-norm of the target against the L1-norm of the last-week counterpart. The positive correlation widens into large scatter at high values, so last week's signal becomes unreliable. Panel (c) plots MAE loss against the L1-norm of the target for Ours (blue) and Baseline (orange). The two curves coincide at low norms. At high norms the baseline error keeps rising while ours plateaus. The eye goes first to the line chart on the left, then to the diverging curves on the right.
caption: Motivating examples on PEMS04 dataset. (a) Varying periodic traffic patterns among connected nodes. (b) Correlation between L1-norms of input and target sequences with respect to their last week counterparts. (c) Performance comparison under growing aperiodicity.
abstract: Accurate traffic prediction is essential for urban planning but remains challenging due to the irregular patterns caused by unexpected events. While Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Networks (STGNNs) effectively model periodic data, they often struggle with these aperiodic fluctuations. To address this, we propose SIMBAD, which improves generalization irregular patterns via two key mechanisms: 1) adaptive regulation of periodic signals to prioritize recent signals, and 2) dynamic spatial modeling that adjusts influence between connected nodes based on contextual relations. Built upon simple similarity metrics to adapt to aperiodic patterns, SIMBAD outperforms existing methods on real-world benchmark datasets, demonstrating superior performance in predicting unseen and irregular traffic events.
